topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its main learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore traditional approaches to eliminating tumors and the associated limitations of systemic toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Targeting Intrinsic Vulnerabilities and Repair Defects in Cancer Cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies that selectively eliminate tumor cells by exploiting their specific genetic defects, checkpoint alterations, and hormone dependencies.

topics.label: Oncogene Targeting and Kinase Inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine small-molecule inhibitors targeting oncogenic driver kinases alongside the mechanisms of acquired drug resistance and pathway bypass.

topics.label: Antibody-Based Cancer Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates target specific cell surface antigens on cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the immune system's capacity to recognize tumors and the clinical approaches used to activate or engineer T cells to attack cancer.

topics.label: Clinical Progress, Challenges, and Future Directions in Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader historical achievements, persistent clinical challenges, and future therapeutic and ethical directions in cancer care.
